name: Clamshell
description: The clamshell is a side-lying hip external rotation exercise in which the feet remain stacked and together while the top knee is raised toward the ceiling, mimicking the opening of a clamshell. It isolates the gluteus medius with a focus on external rotation and abduction, making it one of the most prescribed exercises in physical therapy for hip, knee, and lower back rehabilitation. A resistance band above the knees increases the load.

execution.starting_position: Lie on one side with hips stacked, knees bent to approximately 45°, and feet together. The head rests on the lower arm.
execution.setup_instructions: No equipment needed for bodyweight. Place a mini loop band just above the knees for added resistance.
steps: Step 1: Lie on your side with hips stacked and knees bent at 45°. Keep the feet together throughout.
Step 2: Keeping the feet together, raise the top knee toward the ceiling by externally rotating the hip.
Step 3: Open until the top knee is as high as possible without letting the pelvis roll backward.
Step 4: Hold the peak position, then lower the knee back to the start under control.
Step 5: Complete all reps on one side then switch.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you open the knee. Inhale as you close.
common_mistakes: Rolling the pelvis backward to increase range — the hip should rotate, not the spine
Raising the knee so high that the pelvis tilts — control the range
Using momentum instead of a slow, controlled movement
safety_considerations: Very low-risk exercise suitable for all fitness levels
Often prescribed in rehabilitation for IT band syndrome, patellofemoral pain, and hip pain
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Open the knee as far as possible without pelvic roll. Quality of rotation matters more than range.
coaching_cues: Open like a clamshell — feet stay touching
Don't let the pelvis roll back — keep the hips stacked
Squeeze the glute at the top
